recipes.name: Risotto Tricolore inspired by Big Night
ingredients: 1/2 cup dry white wine, preferably Italian
To taste freshly ground black pepper
1/4 cup extra virgin olive oil (+ more if needed)
instructions: For Risotto:
For the Pressure Cooker Method
Add unsalted butter and olive oil to the bowl of a pressure cooker. Turn the pressure cooker on high to melt the butter - 2 tbsp unsalted butter divided - 1 tbsp olive oil divided
Once the pot is heated and the butter is melted, add the chopped onion. Cook the onions until they are translucent and tender, about 3-5 minutes. - ½ large white onion finely chopped
Add the crushed garlic and cook until the garlic is fragrant about 30 seconds - 2 cloves garlic crushed
Add the Arborio rice and saute until the edges of the rice become translucent about 3 minutes. - 1 cup Arborio rice

Add the white wine and stock. Secure the lid of the pressure cooker and cook under high pressure for 4 minutes. - ½ cup dry white wine preferably Italian - 3 ½ cups Stock (Chicken Seafood, and Vegetable)
Manually release the steam from the pressure cooker valve.
Remove the lid and stir vigorously until the risotto comes together.
Add the Parmesan cheese, olive oil, and butter. - ½ Parmesan cheese grated - 1 tbsp unsalted butter divided - 1 tbsp olive oil divided
Season with salt and pepper to taste, and then serve immediately. - To taste kosher salt - To taste freshly ground black pepper
For the Stovetop Method
In a large saucepan, heat butter and olive oil. - 2 tbsp unsalted butter divided - 1 tbsp olive oil divided
Add the chopped onion and cook until translucent and tender, about 3-5 minutes. - ½ large white onion finely chopped
Add the garlic and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds. - 2 cloves garlic crushed
Add the Arborio rice and saute until the edges of the rice become translucent about 3 minutes. - 1 cup Arborio rice
Add the white wine and cook until the liquid is mostly evaporated. - ½ cup dry white wine preferably Italian

Add the heated stock one large ladle-full at a time. Most of the liquid should be evaporated before adding another ladle of stock. Make sure to keep the risotto at a simmer and to stir consistently during the cooking process. - 3 ½ cups Stock (Chicken Seafood, and Vegetable)
After about 15-20 minutes, the risotto should be al dente and all of the stock incorporated.

Turn off the heat, and add the Parmesan cheese, olive oil, and butter. Season to taste with salt and pepper, serve immediately. - ½ cup Parmesan cheese grated - 1 tbsp olive oil divided - 1 tbsp unsalted butter divided
*Note:

To make Seafood Risotto, swap the chicken stock for homemade seafood stock (recipe listed below), and substitute 3 tablespoons lobster butter (recipe listed below) in place of the 1 tablespoon olive oil and 1 tablespoon unsalted butter.
To make Pesto Risotto, swap the chicken stock for homemade vegetable stock, and add ½ cup basil pesto (recipe listed below) to finish.
For the Lobster Butter
Steam the lobster tails and allow the tails to cool slightly before handling them. - 2 medium sized lobster tails
Remove the lobster meat from the shells (reserve) and devein tails.
Roughly chop the lobster meat and then, place it in a food processor. Process the meat until pureed and reserve.
Over a double-boiler, melt the butter. - 1 stick unsalted butter
Finely chop the reserved lobster shells. Add the shells to the melted butter and cook for an additional 10 minutes.
Removed the butter from the heat and strain through a double layer of cheesecloth or a clean dishtowel. (Be careful as this mixture will be hot and sharp from the shells.)
Chill the butter over an ice bath and add the reserved chopped lobster meat.
Stir to combine and reserve in the fridge until ready to use.
For the Basil Pesto

Combine basil leaves, garlic, pine nuts, Parmesan cheese, salt, pepper, and about ½ of the extra virgin olive oil in the base of a food processor. Process the pesto until well combined and homogenous. - 1 cup (packed) basil leaves - 2 cloves large garlic - 3 tbsp pine nuts toasted - ¼ cup Parmesan cheese grated - 1 tsp kosher salt - ½ tsp freshly ground black pepper - ¼ cup extra virgin olive oil (+ more if needed)
Slowly add the remaining olive oil until the mixture becomes fluid but not overly liquidy.
Reserve the pesto in an airtight container until ready to use.
For Seafood Stock:
For the Seafood Stock
On a large rimmed baking sheet, add prawn shells and toss with olive oil. - 1 pound prawn shells - 2 tbsp olive oil divided
Roast the shells at 375°F for 10 minutes or until red.

In a large pot, heat another tablespoon of olive oil over medium-high heat. Add carrots, onion, and celery and cook until lightly browned about 5 minutes. - 1 tbsp olive oil divided - 2 carrots roughly chopped - 1 large onion quartered - 2 celery stalks roughly chopped
Add the tomato paste and cook for 1 minute. - ¼ cup tomato paste
Deglaze the pot with the white wine and stir to combine. - 1 cup dry white wine

Add the water, roasted prawn shells, parsley, garlic, peppercorns, and bay leaves. - 2 quarts water - 1 pound prawn shells - 7 parsley leaves and stems - 1 garlic head halved - 1 tbsp black peppercorns - 2 bay leaves
Simmer the stock for 45 minutes. Use immediately, or chill the stock over an ice bath and refrigerate until ready to use.
For Chicken Stock:
Add roughly chopped and peeled aromatics like celery, carrots, leek, parsnip, onions, turnip, and garlic. - Celery - Carrots - Parsnips - Leeks - Turnips - Garlic (entire head) - White onions
Along with the vegetables, add in some chopped leftover chicken spine or neck. If not available, chicken wings work. - Chicken spines or wings
In a large pot, add oil and bring to a shimmer then add in the chicken bones/wings and brown. - Vegetable or canola oil - Chicken spines or wings
Once the chicken begins to brown, add in the vegetables, fresh herbs, and peppercorns. - Fresh thyme - Fresh parsley - whole peppercorns
Bring stock to a bare simmer skimming any scum off the top. Simmer for 4-12 hours.
Drain the solids out of the stock and set stock aside but keep warm or chilled until ready to use.
For Vegetable Stock:
For the Vegetable Stock

To make homemade vegetable stock, thinly slice all vegetables using a mandoline. Put all of the vegetable slices in a large bowl and drizzle with vegetable oil. Stir to make sure every piece is evenly coated with oil. - 1 white onion - 4 ribs celery - 1 bulb fennel - 1 parsnip peeled - 3 carrots - 1 leek - 1 small head cauliflower - 2 beets - Vegetable oil

Preheat your oven to 375ºF. Spread vegetable slices out evenly onto 2 large rimmed baking sheets. Roast for anywhere from 30 minutes to 1 hour. Remove from the oven and toss every 15 minutes so that nothing burns.

Add the roasted vegetables to a large dutch oven or stockpot. Add thyme, garlic, parsley, bay leaves, and peppercorns. - Sprigs of fresh thyme - Small head of garlic halved - 1 bunch parsley - 2 dried bay leaves - 1 tbsp whole black peppercorns
Cover with cold water and bring to a simmer. Also add umami boosters now, like dried porcini mushrooms and kombu. - 1 handful dried porcini mushrooms - 2 sheets dried kombu
Let simmer for 45 minutes-1 hour, and then strain.
